A Raízen estuda vender sua divisão de distribuição de combustíveis como parte de um plano mais amplo de venda de ativos, afirmou o acionista e fundador Rubens Ometto à Reuters nesta sexta-feira (27).

"É uma das alternativas que estão sendo consideradas hoje", disse Ometto, que acrescentou que possíveis compradores já analisam o negócio, mas ainda não há um processo formal de venda em andamento.

O empresário não revelou quem são os possíveis interessados nem quanto a Raízen espera receber pela venda.

Reportagens recentes apontaram que o fundo soberano de Abu Dhabi, Mubadala, estaria entre os possíveis interessados na divisão de distribuição de combustíveis da Raízen. Procurado, o fundo não comentou o assunto.

Ometto, que controla a Raízen por meio da Cosan, em parceria com a Shell, disse que ainda não decidiu se fará um novo aporte de capital na empresa como parte de uma reestruturação que reduziria sua participação na produtora de açúcar, etanol e bioenergia.

No início de novembro, a Reuters informou, com base em fontes, que Ometto ainda avaliava a possibilidade de fazer um novo aporte, mas dificilmente investiria mais recursos nas condições econômicas atuais.

Ometto também elogiou a indicação de Luiz Carlos Trabuco, presidente do conselho de administração do Bradesco, para o Ministério da Fazenda, anunciada na quinta-feira (26). Segundo o empresário, a escolha é positiva para a economia brasileira.

"Foi fantástico. Ele é um especialista em finanças e uma pessoa corretíssima", disse Ometto.

No fim de outubro, os acionistas da Raízen aprovaram medidas para viabilizar o plano de recuperação extrajudicial da companhia. Com uma dívida de cerca de R$ 65 bilhões, o processo é considerado a maior recuperação extrajudicial da história do Brasil.

A crise da companhia foi provocada por uma combinação de investimentos arriscados, safras ruins e queda nos preços das commodities.

articles.title: Alvo do governo e do BC, uso do cartão de crédito rotativo se aproxima de R$ 400 bilhões em 2026 e bate recorde | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta semana, o CMN, do qual fazem parte os Ministérios da Fazenda e do Planejamento e o Banco Central, determinou que os bancos terão de reduzir gradualmente o limite de clientes que recorrerem frequentemente ao rotativo do cartão a partir de julho de 2027.
articles.summary: Nesta semana, o CMN, do qual fazem parte os Ministérios da Fazenda e do Planejamento e o Banco Central, determinou que os bancos terão de reduzir gradualmente o limite de clientes que recorrerem frequentemente ao rotativo do cartão a partir de julho de 2027.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Alvo de medidas do governo federal, o uso da linha do rotativo do cartão de crédito, o juro mais alto do mercado financeiro, bateu recorde de uso neste ano.

Segundo dados do Banco Central, as contratações somaram R$ 387 bilhões nos dez primeiros meses de 2026, novo recorde. No mesmo período do ano passado, haviam totalizado R$ 333 bilhões.

As concessões de crédito no cartão rotativo, na parcial de 2026, já se começam a se aproximam do total registrado em todo ano passado — R$ 403 bilhões.

➡️A modalidade, que é considerada um dos vilões do alto nível de endividamento da população brasileira, sofrerá limitação a partir de julho do ano que vem.

Medida do Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN), do qual fazem parte os Ministérios da Fazenda e do Planejamento e o Banco Central, determina que os bancos terão de reduzir gradualmente o limite de clientes que recorrerem frequentemente ao rotativo do cartão.

💳 O objetivo é desestimular o uso recorrente dessa modalidade, uma das mais caras do sistema financeiro. O crédito rotativo do cartão de crédito é acionado por quem não pode pagar o valor total da fatura na data do vencimento.

➡️Segundo o Banco Central, 101 milhões de pessoas no Brasil usavam cartão de crédito no país no começo deste ano. Isso quer dizer que quase a metade do povo brasileiro tem cartão de crédito.

➡️De acordo com a instituição, cerca de 40 milhões de brasileiros estavam com dívida no cartão de crédito rotativo em janeiro deste ano. Até 20 milhões de pessoas podem ser atingida pela limitação de crédito a partir de julho de 2027.

➡️Com juros elevados, a taxa de inadimplência dessa linha de crédito estava em 63,5%, ou seja, mais de R$ 60 em R$ 100 emprestados não foram honrados no começo deste ano.

➡️A taxa de juros do cartão de crédito rotativo, a mais alta de todas, somou 446% ao ano em outubro. No crédito consignado, por exemplo, as taxas variam de cerca 28,3% a 54,9% ao ano.

➡️Segundo analistas, essa forma de crédito deve ser evitada. A recomendação é que os clientes bancários paguem todo o valor da fatura mensalmente.

Em janeiro de 2024, o Congresso e o governo limitaram o endividamento do cartão de crédito rotativo. Desde então, ficou determinado que o valor do débito não pode exceder o valor original da dívida.

Se a dívida for de R$ 100, por exemplo, a dívida total, com a cobrança de juros e encargos, não poderá exceder R$ 200.

De acordo com dados do Banco Central, entre 2012 e 2020, a concessão de crédito (desembolsos) por meio do cartão de crédito rotativo não tinha ultrapassado R$ 225 bilhões em um ano. As variações anuais intercalaram períodos de altas e baixas.

O ano de 2020, principalmente, e de 2021 foram marcados pelo pagamento do Auxílio Emergencial, valores excepcionais pagos à população durante a pandemia, para permitir o afastamento social.

Os dados do cartão de crédito mostram que, no período que coincide com a saída da pandemia e retorno de um patamar mais pesado de inflação, as concessões do cartão de crédito rotativo dispararam.

➡️Com o fim do Auxílio Emergencial a partir de 2022, as concessões de novos empréstimos no cartão de crédito rotativo alcançaram novos patamares, atingindo mais de R$ 400 bilhões em 2025.

➡️Esse período pós-pandemia também foi marcado por fortes pressões inflacionárias, com o índice oficial atingindo mais de 10% em 2021, a maior em seis anos, e cerca de 5,8% em 2022.

Em março deste ano, o presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo, afirmou que as pessoas estão tomando linhas de crédito que deveriam ser usadas somente em momentos emergenciais, como o rotativo do cartão de crédito, como parte de sua renda, e isso deveria ser alvo de uma "discussão estrutural".

"Nossa dimensão do BC é como a gente consegue construir alternativas para o cliente ter uma opção mais adequada à situação dele", disse o presidente do BC, Gabriel Galípolo.

De acordo com Galípolo, a ideia é tentar "produzir arranjos mais saudáveis para quem está buscando crédito", ou seja, linhas de crédito mais adequadas.

Para facilitar a concessão do crédito com taxas menores, o governo lançou, no ano passado, por exemplo, o crédito consignado para trabalhadores do setor privado, com R$ 130 bilhões liberados até junho deste ano.

A expectativa de vida no Brasil chegou a 76,9 anos em 2025 , segundo dados do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ) divulgados nesta sexta-feira (27).

Em 2024, o indicador era de 76,6 anos. Isso representa um aumento de cerca de quatro meses em um ano.

Em 1940, a expectativa de vida ao nascer no Brasil era de 45,5 anos. O indicador avançou ao longo das décadas, ultrapassando os 70 anos em 2000 e chegando a 76,2 anos em 2019. Durante a pandemia de Covid-19, recuou para 72,8 anos em 2021.

A partir de 2022, o indicador voltou a subir e, em 2023, superou o nível registrado antes da pandemia. Entre 1940 e 2025, a expectativa de vida aumentou 31,4 anos. (veja a evolução abaixo)

O levantamento do IBGE também mostra quantos anos uma pessoa pode esperar viver, em média, a partir de determinada idade. Quem tinha 20 anos em 2025, por exemplo, poderia viver, em média, mais 58,4 anos, chegando aos 78,4 anos.

Para quem tinha 40 anos, a expectativa era de mais 40 anos de vida, chegando aos 80 anos. Já entre as pessoas de 60 anos, a estimativa era de mais 22,7 anos, o que corresponde a uma idade de 82,7 anos.

articles.title: Cautious consumers gear up for Black Friday as inflation woes bite
articles.summary: Neither high fuel prices nor stubborn inflation are expected to stop U.S. shoppers from spending robustly as ​their turkey hangovers wear off on Black Friday.
articles.body: NEW YORK/LOS ANGELES — Neither high fuel prices nor stubborn inflation are expected to stop U.S. shoppers from spending robustly as ​their turkey hangovers wear off on Black Friday. But below healthy top-line forecasts lie signs of stress. Holiday spending — which unofficially begins on ‌Black Friday — is seen topping last year’s strong figures by 4%-6%, several economic forecasts show. But most of the gains will be attributable to inflation which, at 3.8%, is about a percentage point higher than in each of the last two years. The National Retail Federation sees November-December holiday retail sales rising 4.2% year-over-year, to just above $1 trillion. The Mastercard Economics Institute and EY Parthenon ​each forecast sales to rise more than 5%. Eventual final results often beat pre-holiday estimates. Still, consumer sentiment remains shaky. This month, voters punished President ​Donald Trump for an Iran War that’s pushed the cost of living higher, handing Democrats sweeping electoral victories. A November survey by ⁠the National Retail Federation found that 82% of consumers are taking steps to manage holiday costs, like buying less expensive gifts. Los Angeles resident Felicia Cox, 50, said ​that while her holiday spending will be roughly stable, inflation is impacting how she thinks. “I want to get more gifts that people will actually use or need,” said ​Cox, a sales representative, while browsing in an L.A. Marshalls last week. “I feel like people aren’t able to afford as much stuff.” Worries aside, some 87% of 1,200 consumers surveyed by Deloitte in October planned to participate in the five-day shopping period from Thanksgiving through “Cyber Monday,” November 30 — the highest in a decade, according to Deloitte. “People like to spend during the holidays,” even ​when there’s a “persisting undercurrent of stress,” said Katie Thomas, who leads the Kearney Consumer Institute, part of global consulting firm Kearney. Middle- and lower-income shoppers — who have ​been trading down for months — were however more likely than wealthy ones to spend less, according to the Kearney survey. Target, Dollar Tree and Kohl’s have all pointed to belt-tightening during recent ‌earnings calls. ⁠Kohl’s CEO Michael Bender on Tuesday cited an “increasingly choiceful” consumer that is “looking to stretch every dollar.” Holiday spending forecasts mostly predated the recent stock market correction that followed the midterms, turmoil at chipmaker Nvidia, and mounting concerns around an AI bubble. The decline could dampen the wealth effect that has seen affluent shoppers splurge on gadgets and accessories, UBS analysts said in a note on Tuesday. Toys take a hit Higher input costs, particularly from petrol derivatives like plastic, are hitting some products more than others. Prices of ​toys — generally high in plastic — have risen ​13.2% since the start of the ⁠year, pushing Barbie maker Mattel this month to cut its annual forecast as consumers balked at higher costs. Some unlikely products are buoying the toy category. Best Buy and Target have both flagged trading cards — including Pokemon and Magic: The Gathering products — as a key ​growth driver. Squishy NeeDoh toys were selling for $24.99 on Amazon in October, nearly triple the price a year earlier ​on hot demand, according ⁠to e-commerce marketing platform Omnisend. Toy maker Learning Resources Inc — a plaintiff in lawsuits that overturned Trump’s tariffs — is seeing demand roughly flat, said CEO Rick Woldenberg, though he added it’s hard to predict demand before Black Friday. “People can’t shop until they have their turkey,” Woldenberg said. AI could also scramble the year’s shopping dynamics. As shoppers use AI ⁠to find bargains ​or even complete purchases — and retailers become increasingly adept at altering price quickly through AI — the deepest ​discounts could come closer to Christmas, as consumers and retailers both wait out the market, said Ryan Orabone, a consultant at Spaulding Ridge. “My advice to shoppers is to be patient,” he said. “Don’t jump on ​the first deal you see.”

articles.title: I let Siri listen to my conversations for weeks. Here’s what it got right — and very wrong
articles.summary: Apple’s new Siri Recap feature can monitor conversations using the latest Apple Watches and generate summaries.
articles.body: I found something surprising when I opened my iPhone’s Siri app last weekend: a summary of a private conversation with my husband. The summary itself wasn’t the surprising part; I turned on a new Apple Watch feature that, with my permission, passively takes notes on conversations. What shocked me, however, was that it was wrong about a key health-related detail in our chat. The new feature, called Siri Recap, can monitor conversations and generate high-level summaries. The idea is to have Siri be like a personal assistant that can jot down details you may have forgotten during a meeting, lecture or conversation, like an action item or TV show recommendation from a friend. It’s part of Apple’s push to make its products more personal and helpful with artificial intelligence, an ambition that got off to a rocky start after Siri faced multiple delays. The iPhone maker is racing against other tech giants to create sophisticated AI assistants that can better understand users’ daily lives, both online and off. But Apple is looking to avoid the privacy concerns raised by its rivals. Siri Recap doesn’t record or save audio, nor does it identify speakers or produce a full transcript. However, because it has less information on users, the Siri Recap summaries aren’t as useful compared to other AI tools. And some experts still take issue with the feature, saying capturing audio at all – even if it isn’t stored – is worrisome. Siri Recap is currently in beta, which means Apple is still updating and improving it, and the company has not yet said when it will launch more broadly. It’s compatible with the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, which must be paired with an iPhone 16 or later, not including the iPhone 16e. Not recording, but still capturing The idea of Siri listening in on conversations would surely raise privacy concerns. So, Apple created a system that it claims can prevent anyone, including itself, from obtaining audio captured by the watch. The Apple Watch captures audio in a secure section of the smartwatch’s processor that’s kept separate from other computing operations. The audio is then shared with the iPhone, which keeps this data separate, and translated into a condensed text version. That shortened version is then sent to Apple’s cloud computing platform where it’s summarized. The audio is discarded before it leaves a user’s phone and is never saved, Apple says. Beyond how the data is handled, Apple keeps its recaps intentionally vague. Unlike other AI wearables, Siri doesn’t provide a full transcript, and most of the time it omits specific names and details. That has its pros and cons. It feels much less intrusive than other AI gadgets I’ve tested, like the Amazon Bee bracelet and Plaud NotePin S, both to myself and the people around me. But there’s also less transparency. Smart glasses and recording accessories light up to indicate when they’re recording, though those lights aren’t always easy to see. The Apple Watch, on the other hand, doesn’t have a visual indicator when it’s activated because it’s not actually recording. It can also be harder to explain Siri Recap. When I record interviews at work or use a device like Bee, I usually ask the people I’m with for consent. But Siri Recap is more challenging to describe since it’s not producing a recording or transcript. And since it’s on until I turn it off, I’ve accidentally captured private conversations I didn’t want summarized. The proliferation of wearable gadgets that can record or document conversations – like watches, glasses and pins – could create broader unease in public, experts say. “That’s going to change interactions, if everybody’s worried about somebody wearing a wire at all times,” said Irina Raicu, director of the internet ethics program at Santa Clara University’s Markkula Center for Applied Ethics. Siri as a notetaker As for the question of whether these recaps are actually useful: They’re sort of like AI-generated summaries but for real life instead of news articles or phone notifications. You can get the gist of the conversation, but it’s not always going to highlight the information you’re looking for, and sometimes it’s inaccurate. The summaries, which range in length depending on the conversation, were helpful at times. One recap of a chat with a colleague included a detail I wanted to include in an upcoming story that I may have otherwise forgotten. Another summary mentioned a musical artist I recommended to a friend during karaoke, reminding me to text them about it. And when I showed a meeting recap to a coworker who couldn’t attend, she said the overview gave her a good gist of what she had missed. The problem, though, is that it’s hard to extract much value from these summaries on most occasions. Keeping things vague preserves privacy, but it also makes the recaps far less informative and often too vague to be useful. One log titled “Thanksgiving Week Work and Family Plans,” for example, has a bullet point that just says: “Reassurance given that there will be enough food.” There are also concerns about whether the information Apple chooses to omit could unintentionally alter the meaning of a summarized conversation. “So much of the meaning of conversations comes in those suggestions and tones, and you know whatever they deem non-essential language,” said Raicu. The summaries also aren’t always accurate. One recap said I was at music trivia when I was actually at a karaoke party. Another time, it misunderstood a story a friend told me about an acquaintance who was helping produce a musical in Los Angeles. Siri thought I was the one producing the show. Other times, Siri recapped dialogue from a TV show or video game – which could be useful. But it was presented the same way as a real conversation in the Siri app, which can be confusing. Siri Recap’s limitations may not matter right now; it only works on certain Apple Watches and iPhones, and people can simply choose not to use it at all. But it speaks to the broader challenge Apple faces in the AI race: How do you make a personal assistant that knows more about you while still preserving privacy? It may be impossible to do both, according to Calli Schroeder, director of the AI and human rights program at the Electronic Privacy Information Center. “Consider the bigger impact on society when suddenly you have to be concerned that anywhere you go, any conversation you have, any interaction with a friend or loved one, could be being processed through this technology,” she said.

articles.title: ‘I cannot go to work’: Iranians contend with pollution as well as US war
articles.summary: Hospital admissions for respiratory ailments have soared as the winter smog sets in.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – The headaches, shortness of breath and blurred vision which Ghoral, 40, a Tehran resident, once only experienced during the heavily polluted, cold seasons of the year have become year-round symptoms.

“The nausea hit me even before the Meteorological Organization announces that the air is polluted,” he tells Al Jazeera.

“On heavily polluted days, I try to leave the house as little as possible, which means I sometimes cannot go to work, affecting my income. At the same time, air pollution increases the cost of seeing a doctor and buying the medication I need to manage my breathing problems. All of this is happening simply because I have no choice but to live in a polluted city.”

The threat of American bombs is not the only danger the residents of Iran’s capital city must contend with these days: checking the air quality has become part of everyone’s daily routine.

Weather apps are no longer used primarily to check the forecast for rain or thunderstorms, but rather to view the latest readings on fine particulate matter (PM2.5) – the tiny, airborne particles which can be deadly when breathed in over a prolonged period.

Hossein, 36, a resident of the capital, tells Al Jazeera: “For someone like me, who both lives and works in the city centre, air pollution is no longer just a part of life; it has become life itself.”

There is little anyone can do about it except escape the city as often as possible, particularly during the winter months when pollution is at its worst.

“At the very least, I try to spend my weekends in nearby cities where the air quality is better,” Hossein says.

The second half of the year in Iran has traditionally been a time of what is known as “temperature inversion”. This occurs when a layer of warm air traps cooler air and pollutants close to the ground, preventing them from dispersing.

While pollution has become a year-round problem, it is particularly bad in the winter, when this phenomenon is common, bringing prolonged periods of polluted air to cities and industrial areas.

Other major Iranian cities, including Mashhad, Isfahan, Shiraz, Tabriz and Ahvaz, are also grappling with air pollution.

For more than half of the autumn and winter months, air pollution warnings are regular, advising people with heart and respiratory conditions to take precautions. Children, older people and pregnant women are also advised to stay indoors and avoid outdoor activities.

In Iran, the Meteorological Organization uses a “yellow weather warning” to signal days on which air pollution levels are particularly high. On those days, schools typically cancel outdoor physical education classes.

When pollution levels approach the threshold for an “orange weather warning” – generally associated with an air quality index (on a scale of 0-500) above 140 – additional restrictions may follow. Some employees switch to remote work, traffic restrictions under the odd-even licence plate scheme are imposed to reduce the number of cars on the streets, schools are closed and some university classes move online.

Dr Hadi Yazdani, who works at a medical centre in Isfahan, tells Al Jazeera: “One of the first signs of rising air pollution is an increase in hospital visits by patients with chronic asthma and other respiratory conditions.”

According to figures from the Ministry of Health, hospital visits for these conditions, as well as for heart conditions, rise by as much as 50 percent in the winter. Eye and skin problems also tend to become more common as a result of air pollution.

“Children and older people are particularly vulnerable,” says Yazdani. “They may develop new illnesses or experience a worsening of existing conditions. In addition, because air pollution reduces the circulation of fresh air, respiratory infections such as influenza and COVID also become more prevalent.”

Evidence that hospitals across Iran experience a surge in emergency department visits as a result of air pollution has prompted the country’s Emergency Medical Services Organization to adopt different plans for managing patient demand during the colder months.

As pollution levels worsen, specially equipped buses are deployed in public squares in some of Iran’s major cities. They provide basic treatment for less severe pollution-related conditions, such as shortness of breath and chest pain. The buses are intended both to reduce the need for ambulances to travel across congested cities and to serve as the first point of contact for people seeking medical assistance.

This year, amid concerns that a renewed war with the United States could force schools to close again anyway, the Ministry of Education has also decided to delegate decisions about school closures due to air pollution to local education authorities.

Although air pollution in Iran is caused by both natural events, such as dust storms, as well as industrial and human-made sources, Iran’s Department of Environment has focused its efforts on tackling pollution caused by human activity.

Ahmad Taheri, head of the National Center for Air and Climate Change at the Department of Environment, tells Al Jazeera: “Alongside efforts to improve the standards of petrol and diesel used by vehicles, we are putting pressure on car manufacturers to produce vehicles that meet higher standards. We are also working to reduce gas flaring at refineries, which contributes both to air pollution and global warming.”

However, the efforts of Iran’s environmental authorities have done little to reassure the public about the country’s air pollution problem.

Every year, as concentrations of air pollutants rise and public health concerns mount, advertisements for vitamins and fresh food products marketed as protective against the effects of air pollution have become increasingly common.

But Yazdani says there is little substantial research demonstrating that vitamins can reduce the health effects of air pollution. He notes that people tend to experience more mood-related problems on polluted days and believes that advertisers are capitalising on public anxiety about the impact of air pollution on health.

The World Health Organization estimates that 99 percent of the world’s population lives in places where air quality falls below the levels it recommends. Knowing this, however, does little to ease people’s concerns about the toll that air pollution is taking on their physical and mental health and Iranians are turning to anything they can find that might help.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty ended sharply lower on Friday, snapping a two-day rally, as rising crude oil prices, profit-booking and concerns over global developments weighed on investor sentiment.The 30-share BSE Sensex plunged 989.33 points, or 1.17%, to settle at 83,339.26. The NSE Nifty 50 declined 277.30 points, or 1.07%, to close at 25,607.20.The selloff gathered momentum through the session, with the Sensex falling 339 points in early trade before extending losses.By 1:57 pm, it was down 749.09 points at 83,579.50, while the Nifty had declined 208.55 points to 25,675.90.Markets retreated after a sharp recovery over the previous sessions, prompting investors to book profits at higher levels. The decline came after the Sensex and Nifty gained on Thursday, extending their rally for a second consecutive session.Most broader market indices ended in the red, while the majority of sectoral indices also closed lower. Nifty Chemicals, Metal, Consumer Durables, MidSmall IT & Telecom, and Media were among the sectors that bucked the trend.On the BSE, BEL, Titan, Trent, Tata Steel and IndiGo were among the top gainers. HCL Tech, TCS, Infosys, Maruti, Tech Mahindra, Axis Bank, Kotak Bank, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Bharti Airtel and ITC were among the major laggards.Why did the market fall?A renewed rise in crude oil prices weighed on the sentiment, with escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East raising concerns over possible supply disruptions.Brent crude climbed above $96.50 a barrel in Asian trade, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude moved towards $85 a barrel.“On the commodities front, WTI crude has extended its advance toward USD 85 a barrel, with renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East adding to supply concerns,” Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, an online trading and wealth-tech firm, told PTI.“While there has been no meaningful disruption to physical supply so far, the market is increasingly pricing in the risk of future disruptions, particularly in a region that accounts for a significant share of global oil flows. With the OPEC+ meeting approaching and tensions across the Gulf remaining elevated, Brent is likely to remain well supported, and any further escalation could keep risk premiums elevated in the near term,” Kaynat Chainwala, AVP Commodity Research, Kotak Neo, told ANI.Rupee also gave up some of its recent gains on Friday as weakness in domestic equities and renewed interest in AI-linked markets threatened to affect foreign investment flows.Rupee opened marginally lower at 92.52 against the US dollar and weakened to 92.9925 before closing at 92.99, down 0.6% on the day. It recorded weekly losses of 0.3%, after gaining 1.7% in the previous week.Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 5,843.33 crore on Thursday, according to exchange data. US equity markets remained closed on Thursday for a holiday.Earlier on Thursday, the Sensex climbed 390.31 points, or 0.46%, to settle at 84,328.59. articles.title: India's non-alcoholic beverage market to hit Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30: Report
articles.summary: India's non-alcoholic ready-to-drink (RTD) beverage market is expected to grow at an annual rate of around 13% to reach Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30, driven
articles.body: India's non-alcoholic ready-to-drink (RTD) beverage market is expected to grow at an annual rate of around 13% to reach Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30, driven by rising demand for energy drinks, protein-based beverages and advanced hydration products, according to a Dolat Capital report.The market, estimated at Rs 1.40 lakh crore in FY26, is witnessing a shift from traditional refreshments towards beverages offering health and functional benefits. Energy drinks and advanced hydration products are expected to grow at more than twice the industry's overall rate, prompting consumer goods companies to expand their presence in these segments.Energy drinks are projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 25.6% between FY26 and FY31, while advanced hydration products are expected to expand at 30.2%, the report said.The energy drinks market is estimated to grow from Rs 9,300 crore in FY26 to Rs 29,000 crore by FY30. Meanwhile, the advanced hydration segment is expected to expand from Rs 4,200 crore to Rs 15,800 crore over the same period.Companies are increasingly targeting consumers looking for beverages that offer more than just refreshment, including products for sports, electrolyte replenishment and recovery, ANI reported.Hindustan Unilever (HUL) and Tata Consumer Products have entered the advanced hydration segment, reflecting growing interest in functional beverages.Protein-based beverages are also gaining traction as companies seek to make protein consumption part of everyday diets rather than limiting it to traditional nutrition supplements.The report noted that "Protein is moving from supplements to everyday beverage", with companies expanding their offerings to include ready-to-drink protein products aimed at regular consumers.Demand for low-sugar alternatives is also growing, prompting companies to introduce zero-sugar variants across beverage categories.The shift towards health-focused consumption is not limited to beverages. Consumer companies are also expanding into protein-rich foods, convenient ready-to-eat products and ingredient-led personal care offerings.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: How India can secure its energy future without trying to eliminate oil, LPG, LNG imports
articles.summary: By Amit Kumar India’s energy-security strategy is increasingly a portfolio of diversified imports, domestic production, strategic reserves, cleaner
articles.body: By Amit KumarIndia’s energy-security strategy is increasingly a portfolio of diversified imports, domestic production, strategic reserves, cleaner substitutes and a more flexible power system. The next step is to connect these initiatives into a measurable resilience framework.Energy security is sometimes confused with race to eliminate imports. For India, that would be an expensive and potentially misleading benchmark. A large, fast-growing economy is more secure when energy remains available and affordable not only in normal times but through geopolitical disruptions, commodity-price shocks, extreme weather and technology transitions. That requires multiple suppliers and routes, strategic stocks, domestic production where competitive, efficient demand and alternatives that can achieve scale.This is broadly the direction of current government policy. Oil and gas measures emphasise exploration, supplier diversification, refining, pipelines and strategic reserves. It also includes: household policy supporting LPG access; electricity generation through non-fossil fuel, transmission, storage and domestic manufacturing on solar cell, batteries, electrolyser etc. The policy architecture is substantial. The remaining challenge is execution across institutions and measuring security by outcomes—days of cover, route concentration, contract flexibility, grid reliability and affordability—not capacity announcements alone.Oil: high import exposure, balanced by refining strengthIndia’s most visible vulnerability is crude oil. In FY2025-26, domestic crude production was about 28 million tonnes and import dependence reached 88.7%, according to the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC). Yet the same system has a major strength: installed refining capacity of 258.1 million tonnes a year and petroleum-product output of 284.9 million tonnes in FY2025-26. India is therefore heavily dependent on imported crude, but comparatively capable in processing, product supply and exports.Government policy addresses the domestic-supply side through the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy and Open Acreage Licensing Program, which offer a uniform licensing framework and allow companies to propose exploration blocks. These reforms may moderate import dependence, but geology, project economics and long development cycles mean that domestic exploration should be treated as one hedge rather than a promise of self-sufficiency.The second hedge is diversification. India now buys crude from a wider set of producers, while refiners retain flexibility to alter grades and suppliers. This reduces single-country exposure, although shipping chokepoints—especially the Strait of Hormuz—remain material. A cargo sourced farther away may improve route security but increase freight, insurance and working-capital costs. For businesses, resilience therefore has a price that should be compared with the cost of disruption.The third hedge is inventory. Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited operates 5.33 million tonnes of strategic storage at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur. The Government has approved a second phase of 6.5 million tonnes at Chandikhol and Padur through public-private partnership models. Commercial inventories held by refiners add another layer. The policy gap is not only storage volume: India also needs transparent release triggers, coordinated emergency exercises and a clear method for rotating stocks without distorting markets.LPG: physical supply and refill affordability must be managed togetherLPG is a special case because energy security reaches directly into household welfare. India consumed roughly 31 million tonnes in FY2025-26; domestic production was about 13.1 million tonnes, leaving close to three-fifths of demand dependent on imports, according to PPAC. Gulf suppliers remain important, so supply disruption and freight costs can quickly affect the subsidy bill and retail affordability.The Government’s response combines import diversification, coastal and inland infrastructure, and the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), which has expanded access to clean cooking fuel. PMUY had released more than 10 crore connections by 2024, according to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.Connections, however, are not the same as sustained use. Refill affordability, last-mile delivery and household cash flow determine whether LPG displaces traditional fuels.A proportionate next step would be to maintain geographically distributed LPG stocks, widen supplier and contract options, and target fiscal support toward vulnerable households rather than suppressing prices across the market.Natural gas and LNG: infrastructure exists, but flexibility is unevenIndia consumed 68.5 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas in FY2025-26. Net domestic production was 34.3 bcm and LNG imports were 34.2 bcm, implying import dependence of about 50%, according to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). As of March 2026, India had eight operational LNG terminals with 53.5 million tonnes per annum of regasification capacity and 27,905 km of operational natural-gas pipelines.These figures show that the constraint is not simply terminal capacity. Utilisation differs sharply by location because pipeline connectivity, anchor demand, delivered prices and contractual commitments vary. Government plans to expand the national gas grid and city-gas networks can improve market depth, but new infrastructure needs credible demand and open, predictable access.LNG security requires a balanced procurement book:long-term contracts for essential demand, multiple pricing benchmarks and origins, destination flexibility, and a measured spot-market allocation. India should also complete technical and commercial assessments for underground or depleted-field gas storage. Gas is not automatically a ‘secure’ transition fuel if buyers remain exposed to spot prices without seasonal buffers.Renewables: “the strategic hedge” now depends on grids and storageRenewables reduce exposure to imported fuels because sunlight and wind have no international commodity price. By 31 October 2026, India had 303.5 GW of renewable capacity, including 174.5 GW of solar, 59.5 GW of wind and 57.5 GW of large and small hydro. Total non-fossil capacity, including nuclear, was 312.2 GW, according to the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).This progress sits within India’s announced goal of 500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030. Supporting programs include Green Energy Corridors, interstate transmission planning, renewable purchase obligations, production-linked incentives for high-efficiency solar modules, PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar and competitive procurement of hybrid and storage-backed power. These are different instruments and are at different implementation stages.Injection of such high capacity of renewables will require power storage of significant capacity and very soon. Central Electricity Authority (CEA) planning estimates that the system may require 47.24 GW (236 GWh) of battery storage and 26.69 GW of pumped storage by 2031-32. Meeting that requirement will depend on viable revenue models, timely transmission expansion, faster approvals, domestic supply chains and flexible demand. Similarly, domestic solar module assembly has scaled but upstream solar materials, battery minerals and power electronics can create new import concentrations. Energy security therefore requires diversified clean-technology supply chains and recycling, not merely more installations.What India can learn from global examplesJapan demonstrates that an import-dependent economy can build resilience through layered public and private oil stocks, mandatory industry obligations and tested emergency procedures. India need not copy Japan’s inventory scale; the transferable lesson is clear governance across strategic and commercial stocks.The European Union’s post-crisis gas policy uses seasonal storage targets, monitoring and burden-sharing to reduce winter risk. India’s climate, geology and gas-market structure differ, but minimum inventory rules for selected users and strategic storage pilots could be adapted after cost-benefit analysis. Denmark shows another principle: high shares of variable renewables are easier to manage with strong interconnection, flexible demand and regional balancing.India’s equivalent is deeper interstate coordination and a transmission system that treats balancing resources as national assets.The outlookIn the next two to three years, priority should be to completing approved petroleum-reserve expansion, strengthening LPG and gas contingency protocols, improving utilisation of existing LNG and pipeline assets, and accelerating already-planned transmission and energy storage projects. The government should publish a compact energy-security dashboard covering import concentration, route exposure, stock cover, contract mix, grid congestion and affordability.Through 2030 and 2032, the emphasis should shift toward structural demand reduction: efficient vehicles and industry & public transport electrification, rooftop and distributed power, ethanol and biogas where sustainably supplied, and a grid capable of integrating the official non-fossil pipeline. Policy should remain technology-neutral about reliability: batteries, pumped hydro, hydro, nuclear, flexible thermal generation and demand response can each play roles with different costs and lead times.Total energy security is therefore better understood as the ability to absorb a shock without severe economic or social disruption. India’s plans already contain most of the necessary building blocks. The expert test is whether they are delivered in the right sequence, operated as one system and evaluated against resilience and affordability, not whether imports fall to zero.(The author, Amit Kumar, is Partner and Climate Ecosystem Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat)Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: US shoppers get ready for Black Friday and Cyber Monday
articles.summary: Cyber Monday and Black Friday compete for shoppers, but discounts on electronics may peak after the weekend frenzy.
articles.body:
Across the United States, retailers are gearing up for some of their biggest sales of the year on Black Friday and Cyber Monday, enticing bargain hunters with slashed prices and promises of hefty savings.

For some shoppers, the Thanksgiving leftovers will barely have made it into the fridge before they bundle up in their coats and head to big-box store car parks, queuing in the predawn darkness in hopes of snapping up a bargain on a pair of jeans, a doll, a toy truck or a new laptop.

The day after Thanksgiving has become known as Black Friday and is the unofficial start of the holiday shopping season, though many retailers began rolling out their discounts weeks ago.

This year, however, the annual shopping frenzy comes against a backdrop of economic uncertainty. Household budgets are increasingly stretched and Americans have to weigh their holiday wish lists against the rising cost of everyday necessities.

So, how did Black Friday evolve into a global retail phenomenon, how much are shoppers expected to spend this year and are the bargains really as good as they seem?

The marriage of Thanksgiving and holiday shopping in the United States stretches back more than a century. In 1924, Macy’s launched its Thanksgiving Day Parade, transforming the streets of Midtown Manhattan into a spectacle of festive fanfare to entice shoppers into its department store. This year is the 100th edition of the parade, which was suspended during World War II. However, inclement weather forced the retailer to postpone this year’s festivities until Saturday, the first time in 55 years.

By 1939, the Christmas shopping season had become so economically significant that President Franklin D Roosevelt moved Thanksgiving from November 30 to November 23. That gave retailers an extra week to ring up sales and stimulate consumer spending amid an economic downturn. The change, however, was short-lived. In 1941, Congress established the fourth Thursday of November as the permanent date for the Thanksgiving holiday.

But the term Black Friday has considerably darker origins, dating back to the 1860s, when it had nothing to do with shopping or the Thanksgiving holiday. In September 1869, financiers Jay Gould and James Fisk attempted to corner the US gold market. Their scheme unravelled spectacularly, sending gold prices tumbling and plunging Wall Street into financial turmoil.

The term resurfaced in the 1950s, this time on the streets of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Police officers began using it to describe the gridlocked streets and general chaos brought on by the hordes of shoppers and football fans descending on the City of Brotherly Love following Thanksgiving, ahead of the annual Army-Navy football game.

By the 1980s, retailers had found a way to turn the once-unflattering moniker into a marketing tool. In accounting, being “in the black” means turning a profit. Retailers capitalised on that association, recasting Black Friday as a lucrative shopping event and distancing it from its more chaotic origins.

While Black Friday is a distinctly US invention, the shopping frenzy has long since transcended US borders, becoming a global phenomenon at shopping centres and digital storefronts around the world.

How has Cyber Monday fared against Black Friday?

Despite the rise of Cyber Monday – when online retailers slash prices – Black Friday remains the main event. Some 126 million Americans are expected to shop on Friday, compared with 66.1 million on Monday, according to the National Retail Federation (NRF).

After years of shoppers swapping crowded malls and long checkout lines for virtual shopping baskets, the pendulum appears to be swinging somewhat back in favour of physical retail. While online shopping remains the most popular option for holiday shoppers, 53 percent say they plan to shop online this season, the lowest proportion since 2015.

Americans also expect to complete 52 percent of their holiday shopping online, down from 56 percent last year and a pandemic-era peak of 60 percent in 2020.

While the bustle of malls and festive window displays are regaining some of their appeal, the digital marketplace is far from losing its dominance among consumers. Some 55 percent of holiday shopping will be online, compared with 45 percent in physical stores, according to accountancy firm Deloitte.

What is the projected holiday spending this year?

Brightly wrapped gifts may look much the same this holiday season, but behind the holiday cheer Americans are keeping a closer eye on their wallets. A tighter economy is forcing consumers to be more selective about what goes into their shopping baskets.

A survey by research firm Gartner found that nearly 60 percent of Americans have less money to spend on the holidays this year than last. To stretch their budgets, many got a head start on ticking off their gift lists, with 57 percent of consumers doing at least some of their holiday shopping in October or earlier.

Americans are not abandoning the tradition of gift-giving altogether, however. Spending on presents is expected to dip by just 2 percent from last year, with millennials making the deepest cuts of any generation, scaling back by 10 percent, according to an analysis by PwC.

Meanwhile, the National Retail Federation expects overall holiday spending to surpass $1 trillion.

How much consumers spend may largely depend on the size of their paycheques. The Conference Board forecasts that consumers earning less than $125,000 a year will rein in their spending on gifts, while those earning more than that plan to spend 3.6 percent more.

A sliver of that holiday spending may be fuelled by the growing popularity of buy now, pay later (BNPL) services offered by financial technology companies such as Klarna and Affirm. The proportion of US consumers using those services climbed from 10 percent in 2020 to 16 percent in 2025, according to the Federal Reserve.

As shoppers fill their virtual baskets, a growing share of those purchases will be paid for in instalments. Nearly $2bn in online purchases will be financed through buy now, pay later services on Black Friday and Cyber Monday alone, Adobe Analytics forecasts.

Do Black Friday and Cyber Monday really spell bargains?

Not always. A recent investigation by the economic think tank Groundwork Collaborative found that, over the past two years, nearly 10 percent of the products Amazon advertised as “deals” during its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales actually carried higher price tags than in the month before those promotions began.

“Groundwork’s claims are false and willfully ignore the facts. They’re based on a review of a mere 350 products, many of which weren’t even deals, versus 10 million deals offered to customers during Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2024 and 2025,” an Amazon spokesperson told Al Jazeera.

“We analyzed the actual deals in Groundwork’s small dataset and found that 98% of the products were the same or lower than the price over the past 30 days—in line with our strict deal guardrails for our deal events.”

Amazon kicked off this year’s Black Friday sales on November 19, dangling discounts of up to 40 percent on some toys, including Lego sets, 35 percent on select electronics and 50 percent on Levi’s clothing.

An analysis of Walmart’s early Black Friday sales this month by Walsight, a Walmart market intelligence platform, found that 23 percent of products advertised at a discount offered little or no meaningful savings compared with their typical selling prices.

But that does not mean bargain hunters will come away empty-handed. Adobe Analytics forecasts that seasonal discounts at major online retailers could reach 30 percent.

For parents on the hunt for toys, discounts are expected to peak at 29 percent on Black Friday, while shoppers eyeing the latest gadgets may be better off waiting until Cyber Monday, when discounts on electronics are forecast to reach 30 percent.

articles.title: Investors fleeing AI stocks may own more of them than they think: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft now top a fund built to avoid pricey growth stocks.
articles.body:
Investors have spent weeks running from AI stocks. Many of the funds they're running to are loaded with them.

The Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ) has tumbled since its Oct. 6 record, twice falling more than 20% below it during the day, the usual line for a bear market , only to rally back before the close. Meanwhile, chip stocks have lost about 40% from their June peak.

One client called up Barbara Doran, CEO and chief investment officer of BD8 Capital Partners, to say, "Get me out of everything." That "would have to be the entire portfolio because every company in that portfolio is using AI," Doran told Yahoo Finance on Wednesday.

The same goes for funds. "If you found yourself nauseous after the last few days of volatility, consider how much Tech exposure you have across a portfolio of ETFs," Todd Sohn of Baird Strategas wrote this week in a note to investors.

So we double-checked. According to Yahoo Finance calculations, the iShares Russell 1000 Value ETF ( IWD ) went from about 11% tech a year ago to nearly 19%. The iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF ( EEM ) went from 26% to 39%. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) didn't budge, at about 35%.

The biggest surprise is in the value fund, the kind meant to steer clear of pricey growth stocks. Its three biggest holdings are now Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), and Microsoft ( MSFT ), which together account for about 17% of the fund. A year ago, it didn't own Apple or Microsoft at all.

Both arrived during FTSE Russell's annual index reshuffle in June.

And 19% undercounts it. Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta don't count as tech under Wall Street's sector rules . Count the "Magnificent Seven," and Big Tech went from about 7% of the fund to 18%.

Emerging markets got the same makeover. Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ), Samsung ( 005930.KS ), and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) now make up about 27% of EEM, up from 16%.

EEM and the iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF ( MTUM ), which loaded up on chip stocks in May, have both fallen harder than the Nasdaq-100 over the past three months.

The value fund has held up, so far. Its new tech is mostly Apple and Microsoft, not chips.

Every fund's Yahoo Finance quote page lists its sector mix under Holdings , and not every value fund looks alike. The Vanguard Value ETF ( VTV ) is about 11% tech, Bloomberg data shows.

Or, as Luka Kawa of Sherwood News put it Tuesday on Market Hang , "Back in June, we are all momentum investors. And now to be successful, you've got to take out your pencil, do a lot of erasing, get Claude to work in Excel for you."

articles.title: Binance lifts withdrawal suspension after $6.3 billion crypto heist
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has completed work to restore its withdrawal systems following last month's $6.3 billion
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has completed work to restore its withdrawal systems following last month's $6.3 billion cyber heist, the company said on Thursday. However, withdrawals on a small number of blockchain networks remain temporarily suspended due to routine maintenance, separate from the security incident."Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted," Binance said in a post on X."Withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. Separately, a small number are temporarily paused due to network maintenance, which is standard practice," it added.The announcement marks the completion of a phased restoration process that began on November 1, after the exchange suspended withdrawals for more than two days following the attack. Customers withdrew a net $4.7 billion from the platform when services first reopened, according to Binance's November 2 update.What happened in the $6.3 billion Binance heist?The cyberattack took place on October 29, when hackers gained unauthorised access to Binance's hot wallets, which are cryptocurrency wallets connected to the internet, and stole tokens worth approximately $6.3 billion. The attackers targeted wallets across 10 different blockchains, with most of the funds transferred within a roughly 20-minute window, according to blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs.Binance's initial investigation pointed to a potentially compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer as an entry point. The company later said it had identified additional points of compromise. The FBI and blockchain intelligence firms linked the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-backed hacking group.Following the breach, Binance temporarily halted withdrawals while it reviewed its security systems and worked to contain the losses. The exchange assured customers that their funds were safe and committed to absorbing the financial impact of the stolen assets.Where do the stolen funds stand?Binance has said it has the financial resources to cover the losses and will not pass the cost on to customers. Meanwhile, approximately $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue the affected tokens.However, blockchain researchers say the remaining funds are being moved through lesser-known cryptocurrency services in an elaborate money-laundering operation. articles.summary: A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.'s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker.

The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia's most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News.

A second firm Shanghai Kezhan, controlled by a Tokyo-based parent, described a GB200 server — which also relies on Blackwell chips — at the facility. That description was provided in documents when it obtained a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a finance-leasing firm wholly owned by a local Shanghai government agency.

The submissions reveal for the first time that Nvidia's Blackwell processors found their way into a Chinese data center that has ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed. These processors were until recently Nvidia's most powerful data center products, and they've always been illegal to ship to China without a US license.

President Donald Trump has explicitly said he doesn't want these chips — which OpenAI and Anthropic PBC use to train their most cutting-edge models — going to the Asian country, at least for now. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, meanwhile, once claimed they were too big to smuggle: a standard two-meter-tall GB300 NVL72 server rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips and 36 Grace processors, can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms (3,300 pounds) and is about the size of a gigantic fridge.

Nvidia and its just-reinstated CEO have come under intense scrutiny in recent weeks for their failure to stop diversion of the company's products to China, a shadow trade that US officials believe is worth billions of dollars.

It's unclear how the GB300 rack made its way to the country, to Shanghai Shuoyao or to this specific site — described in local media as designed to house as many as 800,000 servers. By inputting the serial number for the product into a public warranty database, Bloomberg found that it was manufactured by Taiwan's Gigabyte Technology Co., which assembles Nvidia chips into servers and racks. The database also provided a model name for the serial number, which matches a GB300 NVL72 server rack manufactured by the Taiwanese company.

articles.title: Union Budget 2027: Should government scrap LTCG tax and hike STT instead?
articles.summary: The pre-budget consultation has just wrapped up, and the proposals have put the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax back at the centre of the policy
articles.body: The pre-budget consultation has just wrapped up, and the proposals have put the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax back at the centre of the policy conversation. Industry bodies have largely converged on one demand: that the levy be lowered or removed altogether, though they differ on specifics. SBI, for its part, has floated a graded, slab-style tax structure. The sharpest disagreement among these proposals is over what should happen to the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).With Budget 2027-28 approaching, two conflicting opinions have emerged: SBI Research's Ecowrap report has studied the option of scrapping or reworking the 12.5% equity LTCG tax, a move estimated to cost the exchequer ₹40,000–₹50,000 crore in FY28. To plug that hole, it suggests raising STT by 50%, which would bring in around ₹45,000 crore. PHDCCI argues the reverse. It wants equity LTCG abolished, the Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax halved from 20% to 10%, and STT rates brought down at the same time.Two questions follow. Can a steeper STT genuinely replace the revenue the government would give up on LTCG? And would lighter taxation of gains pull more capital into equities?The same trade, taxed twiceSTT applies to defined securities transactions executed on recognised stock exchanges. What sets it apart from LTCG tax is its base: it has nothing to do with how much an investor earns. Someone who exits a position at a loss still has to pay STT on the sale.That is why industry groups describe equity investors as carrying two distinct burdens. STT is measured against the value of the transaction, whereas LTCG tax is measured against the gain realised when eligible shares are sold after the qualifying long-term holding period.PHDCCI objects that STT paid cannot be subtracted when capital gains are worked out. It therefore wants both taxes reviewed together. In its reading, a non-deductible STT stacked on top of a tax on gains is double taxation, and it erodes the competitiveness of Indian capital markets.FICCI has taken a more balanced line. It would like the LTCG exemption brought back, and it is open to a higher STT on delivery-based trades to make up the revenue shortfall. SBI Research likewise lists an STT hike as one way of financing the abolition of LTCG tax.Where the last budget left thingsUnion Budget 2026 lifted STT on Futures and Options (F&O) from April 1, 2026, with the stated intention of restraining speculative trading and systemic risk. Delivery-based equity trades and mutual fund units escaped any change.Critics of any further hike argue that the derivatives market has little room left to absorb additional costs. As one assessment puts it:Former senior public sector banker Kulvinder Singh Sethi said, “After consecutive increases in STT, derivatives volumes are already sensitive to cost friction. Raising STT by another 50% risks compressing trading activity and liquidity — meaning actual revenue gains can fall short of linear projections while nudging liquidity toward lower-friction instruments or offshore venues.”From enactment to evolution: 22 years of STT reformsThe tax is hardly new. It arrived in 2004 as a substitute for LTCG tax on listed equities, and successive Finance Acts have since pushed it in both directions, sometimes raising rates, sometimes trimming them, and sometimes changing the base on which it is computed.Read in sequence, the timeline shows a broad run of increases in the first two years, a spell of relief around 2012 and 2013, and then, from 2016 onwards, a series of hikes aimed mostly at derivatives.Foreign inflow has not taken the baitOn the revenue front, the latest hikes have clearly delivered. As of September 17, STT collections for 2026-27 stood at ₹40,214.36 crore, up nearly 53% from ₹26,305.72 crore recorded over the same stretch a year before.The jump traces back to the new rates. STT on futures went from 0.02% to 0.05% of traded value. On options, the levy on premium turnover climbed from 0.1% to 0.15%, and the levy on exercised options moved from 0.125% to 0.15% of intrinsic value.However, higher STT has not translated into stronger interest from foreign investors. NSDL data shows net foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows swinging between inflows and outflows through 2026.“FPIs already navigate rupee currency dynamics alongside capital gains tax rules. Because STT is levied as an upfront transaction toll regardless of whether a trade ends in profit or loss, higher STT raises round-trip execution friction for foreign funds running hedged, arbitrage, or cross-market strategies—making competing Asian markets look comparatively cleaner on transaction costs,” Sethi said.Signals from the street and finance ministryThe market's sensitivity to this topic was on display on October 13, 2026. The BSE Sensex climbed by more than 1,100 points and the Nifty 50 gained about 1.6%, adding over 350 points. The catalyst was Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's willingness to hear out stakeholders on LTCG tax and STT in the run-up to the 2027 Budget.At the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, asked whether LTCG tax and STT might be rationalised, she replied: “We are very close to the Budget, and the preparation for the Budget has started. It may not be the best time for me to say what I will or what I will not consider,” and added that she would welcome suggestions on the subject.The rally points to an expectation among investors that the tax framework will be revisited. Some observers stress that the way the revenue gap is bridged counts as much as the relief itself:“From a market-microstructure standpoint, easing transaction friction—or offering calibrated LTCG relief without punitive STT hikes — is far healthier for price discovery than using STT as a mechanical revenue plug,” Sethi said.Sethi added that since STT is charged on the transaction value, regardless of whether you make a profit or incur a loss, increasing the tax rate will lead to penalising liquidity and discouraging market participation.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: RBI lowers minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement from 99% to 90%
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The RBI has cut the required cash reserve ratio requirement from 99% to 90%, effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The RBI has cut the required cash reserve ratio requirement from 99% to 90%, effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026."On the basis of an assessment of the current and evolving macroeconomic situation and liquidity conditions, it has been decided to reduce the minimum daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) from 99 per cent of the requirement to 90 per cent effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026," the RBI said.The move reversed a change introduced by the RBI just over a month earlier. In October, the central bank had raised the minimum daily Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for scheduled banks from 90 per cent to 99 per cent, effective October 16, 2026.Under the revised directive, scheduled banks will have to maintain at least 90 per cent of their prescribed CRR on each day during the reporting fortnight, compared with the earlier minimum of 99 per cent. However, the average CRR maintained over the entire fortnight must still meet the RBI's prescribed requirement.The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the portion of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL), or deposits, that it must keep as cash reserves with the RBI. For instance, at a CRR of 4.5 per cent, banks must deposit Rs 4.50 with the RBI for every Rs 100 of deposits. The remaining Rs 95.50 can be used for lending and other banking operations.The RBI's move lowers the minimum daily maintenance threshold without changing the prescribed CRR rate. This gives banks greater flexibility to manage day-to-day liquidity, as they can hold a smaller proportion of their required reserves on individual days, provided the fortnightly average meets the prescribed level.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nvidia stock is still paying the price for the Jensen Huang CEO drama
articles.summary: Nvidia's stock will need some time to find solid footing.
articles.body:
Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock remains damaged goods despite CEO Jensen Huang being back at headquarters in trademark loafers.

"It's been a traumatic situation for investors. They can't figure out which way is up. So we are going to see volatility," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said on Sozzi Unleashed .

Shares of Nvidia rose more than 2% in premarket trading on Friday, following a 3.9% decline on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving and a 5.86% decline on Tuesday.

The stock popped more than 31% on Monday as investors digested the stunning news of Huang's return as CEO, just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes.

The dramatic reversal of fortunes for Huang followed intense lobbying from President Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who intervened directly with directors and said Huang had been cleared of national security concerns.

Huang said at an all-hands meeting on Tuesday that he was in therapy, but struck a defiant tone on his management style and lack of succession planning.

Despite the initial rally upon his return, Nvidia still faces Justice Department and SEC investigations into alleged chip smuggling through blacklisted Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, which prompted the board to appoint a new chief compliance officer.

Huang is also scheduled to testify before Congress next week, in a closed-door House interview on Dec. 1 and a public Senate Banking Committee hearing on Dec. 3.

Volatility will likely be the name of the game in the near-term for Nvidia investors, Ives says.

"We'll see volatility into next week. Obviously the China hawks are going to be out [when Jensen appears]. The knives are going to be out because of the concerns about where this is all going," Ives added.

articles.title: No interim relief for Tata Trusts: Tata Sons board meeting to be held as scheduled, says HC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Bombay High Court on Friday refused to grant interim relief to two Tata Trusts challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as Tata
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Bombay High Court on Friday refused to grant interim relief to two Tata Trusts challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman for a third five-year term, allowing the company's November 30 board meeting to proceed as scheduled.A bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja said any decision taken at the meeting would remain subject to the court's final orders."We are not granting any relief. today. Let the meeting go on as scheduled. and everything will be subject to further order," the court observed.During Friday's hearing, senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for Tata Sons, opposed the request to defer the meeting, saying the company had to take a decision in view of a Reserve Bank of India directive. The RBI has set December 12 as the deadline for Tata Sons to inform it of its decision on complying with the central bank's listing requirements.Salve argued that any resolution passed at the board meeting would remain subject to the high court's orders. However, senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, representing the SDTT, contended that the RBI directive was being used by Tata Sons to create a sense of urgency and push through the meeting.The trusts had sought a stay or postponement of the November 30 meeting. They also requested an order restraining Chandrasekaran from exercising his casting vote as executive chairman if there was a split among the nominee directors on the board.The court directed Tata Sons and the other respondents, including six of its directors, to file reply affidavits to the two suits and scheduled the next hearing for January 18, 2027.The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the RD Tata Trust (RDTT), which are among the seven charitable trusts controlling the Tata group, filed the petitions challenging Chandrasekaran's reappointment. The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore in damages, while the RDTT has claimed Rs 15 crore, both with 18 per cent annual interest.The trusts have argued that the September 17 board resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran was invalid as it did not secure the affirmative votes required from their nominee directors under Article 121 of Tata Sons' Articles of Association.Tata Trusts, the largest shareholder in Tata Sons, has maintained that the reappointment required the approval of both its nominee directors. One of them is Trusts chairman Noel Tata.Tata Sons, which owns prominent businesses and brands including Jaguar Land Rover and Tetley Tea, reappointed Chandrasekaran in September despite opposition from Noel Tata. The dispute has now moved to the courts, with the two trusts questioning the validity of the decision.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: NBA team ETFs just got filed — here's what Knicks and Lakers fans would actually own
articles.summary: LeagueShares' new NBA funds would hold futures on each team's index.
articles.body:
Buying an NBA team still costs billions. Soon, one ETF share may let fans ride along with a team's season.

LeagueShares refiled for 30 NBA team ETFs this week, this time under the real team names. The lineup includes Knicks, Lakers, and Celtics funds, under proposed tickers KNIX, LALK, and CELT, respectively, that aren't trading yet. The filing can't take effect for 75 days, so the earliest the funds could launch is February. Hockey and baseball team funds are already in the pipeline .

"First-ever basketball ETFs with the actual NBA team names just got filed from LeagueShares," Bloomberg Intelligence's Eric Balchunas posted on X .

The same morning, FutureSports signed an exclusive deal with the NBA for its official stats, which FutureSports will use to build team indexes that CME Group ( CME ) plans to list futures on, pending regulatory review. The filing says the funds aren't licensed or sponsored by the league or its teams.

Not the team, and no courtside seats. Think fantasy basketball with a brokerage statement.

The funds would hold futures on each team's index, which starts every season at 7,500. Points, assists, and wins push it up. Points allowed, turnovers, and losses drag it down. Playoff runs count, and the index resets after the finals.

The filing shows how last season would have scored. The champion Knicks index rose 78%, and the Brooklyn Nets index sank 76%.

Wins explain most but not all of it. The Knicks and Lakers both went 53-29, yet the Knicks index gained 78% and the Lakers 17%. The Clippers missed the playoffs and still rose 14%. The Trail Blazers made the playoffs and fell 35%. FutureSports has since changed its scoring method, so this season will be scored differently.

Add up all 30 teams, and the league went nowhere.

That's by design. Most of the stats are scored against the other team, so every point scored is a point allowed, and every win is somebody's loss.

Add up all 30 indexes, and they finished last season less than 1% from where they started. A stock index can grow along with the economy. This one is a zero-sum game even before fees, which haven't been disclosed, and the cost of swapping expiring futures contracts for new ones.

There's a scheduling catch too. Only eight of last season's 1,322 games overlapped stock market hours, so the indexes move almost entirely while the funds can't trade. The prospectus warns of "large gaps at the open."

Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji told Yahoo Finance earlier this month that the biggest problem he sees in investing today is that "people are blurring the lines between investing and gambling."

articles.title: Swiggy cuts 340 jobs at Instamart
articles.summary: Swiggy lays off 340 Instamart employees in restructuring, mainly mid-senior roles, to cut duplication and boost profitability amid competition and losses.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Swiggy is laying off 340 employees at its quick commerce arm Instamart as part of a restructuring exercise, with the cuts largely affecting mid-to-senior staff, people familiar with the development told TOI. Analytics and category management are among the teams where the layoffs have been concentrated, they said.The cuts follow about three months of unease over job security, according to an employee who described an increasingly uncertain atmosphere within the business. Several colleagues have been looking for jobs elsewhere, the employee said. The person also pointed to pressure on the business amid competition from Blinkit and scrutiny from stock market investors.Swiggy had not responded to TOI’s queries at the time of publication.Another person familiar with the company’s thinking said Instamart was reorganising its teams and ways of working, taking into account the use of generative artificial intelligence. The exercise was aimed at removing duplication, strengthening accountability and speeding up decisions, the person added.The restructuring comes as Instamart seeks to improve profitability while growing its business. Its gross order value, or the total value of orders, rose 16.7% from the preceding quarter to Rs 9,230 crore in the three months ended September, according to Swiggy’s financial disclosures. It added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking its network to 1,240 stores across 133 cities.However, the business remained loss-making. Its adjusted Ebitda loss stood at Rs 895 crore in the September quarter. Swiggy had about Rs 13,500 crore in cash as of the September quarter, one of the sources added.Affected employees will receive severance support in addition to statutory payouts, along with accelerated vesting of employee stock options through their last working day, TOI has learnt. Health insurance and wellness subscriptions will be extended until May 2027.The assistance package also includes relocation support for eligible employees and help finding new jobs, including three months of premium access to career and networking tools.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Anthropic's Dario and Daniela Amodei may have just made a $560 million misstep
articles.summary: Anthropic's stock continues to be very volatile in the wake of its IPO.
articles.body:
The brother-and-sister duo of Dario and Daniela Amodei at Anthropic ( ANT ) may have failed to read the room in the race to become a public company.

"If you have something called emotional intelligence, you could have seen that [the market didn't want them to sell stock]. So the fact that they did that, it's a bad signal as well," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said on Sozzi Unleashed .

The Amodeis each disclosed selling roughly $280 million in shares as part of the IPO, totaling $560 million. Those sales were made to underwriters at the offering price and aren't evidence of some sudden executive exodus.

But the optics won't help investor confidence against a risk-off backdrop for AI stocks. Anthropic shares have been penalized accordingly.

Less than a week after its blockbuster IPO, Anthropic shares fell 8.5% to $80.21 and closed below their $83 IPO price on Wednesday. The stock hit a low of $73.85 on the session.

Shares are rallying back today by 3% to $85 in premarket trading.

Anthropic's stock opened on IPO day at $111.50, briefly topped $115, and carried a valuation north of $2 trillion. Now the stock is down more than 30% from its highs, and the market cap stands at about $1.1 trillion.

Wall Street is also questioning the enormous cost of building AI infrastructure, whether data-center spending can continue to accelerate, and how quickly these companies can turn their technology into sustainable profits.

Ives added, "It's also about pricing. Like my view is OK, fair value is at $1.5 trillion, $1.7 trillion, you know, depending on how they execute. They should have priced it to a point given demand, probably closer to like $1 trillion or $1.1 trillion. I mean, in a market like this, I think that's what's playing out here."
