articles.title: Oil prices are again rising – here’s why
articles.summary: Brent crude futures for January delivery have climbed this week to trade around $96 a barrel, after settling Thursday at their highest point since the week of the midterms.
articles.body: A fresh flare up in tensions in the Middle East is putting the brakes on oil’s recent slide. Front-month Brent crude futures for January delivery have climbed this week to trade around $96 a barrel Friday, after settling Thursday at their highest point since the week of the midterm elections. The global oil benchmark is on track for its first weekly gain this month, rising around 3.5% for the week. Prices remain far off the highs of near $120 a barrel seen at points throughout the war with Iran. But they’ve bounced back after dipping below $90 earlier this week. For weeks, oil prices have been falling – in part because US President Donald Trump held back from escalating military action in the Middle East after the midterms. Flows from the region have also picked up, despite attacks on tankers, and global oil consumption has fallen dramatically. But a fresh wave of attacks in the Middle East has sent prices climbing again in recent days. US-traded West Texas Intermediate oil futures also climbed Friday, rising 1% to trade around $84.50. On Thursday, a suspected Iranian drone attack on a Kuwaiti military site killed two Italian nationals, according to Italy’s foreign minister Antonio Tajani. The individuals were technicians employed by defense firm Rheinmetall Italia. A Kuwaiti national and a Pakistani national were also wounded, Kuwait’s defense ministry said. Iran denied carrying out the attack. Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck two Saudi Arabian oil refineries back-to-back this week – first on Wednesday, when the group claimed to have struck the nation’s biggest oil refinery at Ras Tanura. The following day, a projectile struck an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s southwestern Jazan region, killing a Nepalese worker. The strike sparked a fire and temporarily suspended some operations at the facility, according to the Saudi Ministry of Energy. A skyscraper that houses the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s trillion-dollar sovereign wealth fund in the capital, Riyadh, was also hit for the second time in a matter of days this week, wounding 11 people, according to an eyewitness and Saudi authorities. Iran has continued to strike tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Around two dozen attacks have been reported in November, according to a CNN analysis of data from the UK Maritime Trade Operations Centre, nearing the record 30 attacks set in October. Oil flows through the strait were at 55% of their pre-war level over the week to November 25, preliminary data from Kpler showed Friday, indicating that the attacks are having an effect on transits. “These attacks remind us of the inherent instability of the status quo, as a lasting peace deal between the US and Iran remains elusive,” Kathleen Brooks, research director at online broker XTB wrote in a note Friday. “From a market perspective, a sustained rise in the price of oil… could take the shine off an AI rally later today,” she continued. US stock futures are rising Friday morning, with Nasdaq-100 contracts up more than 2%, following a stretch of volatile trading for tech stocks earlier in the week. The front-month Brent futures contract differs from the also closely watched continuous Brent contract, which traded around $92 Friday. The difference reflects the fact that the front-month contract is more closely tied to the physical oil market, and its higher price points to stronger demand for near-term supplies of crude as refiners work to secure barrels. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, known as OPEC+, will meet Sunday. The group, which meets monthly to set production quotas for members, has held oil output steady since September following six consecutive increases before that. “The group is expected to consider keeping current production quotas unchanged through January, although some members have been pushing for higher quotas,” ING analysts said. – CNN’s Billy Stockwell and Nadeen Ebrahim contributed reporting.

articles.title: Dangerous Nor’easter Storm Triggers US East Coast Power Outages
articles.summary: More than 500,000 homes and businesses along the East Coast are without power after an explosive storm uprooted trees in Queens and inundated commuter rail l...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- More than 500,000 homes and businesses along the East Coast are without power after an explosive storm uprooted trees in Queens and inundated commuter rail lines in New Jersey on Thanksgiving Day.

The nor'easter system that pummeled New York City and surrounding areas also carried heavy rains as far south as North Carolina. Though the storm is losing power Friday, beaches from Virginia to Maine are still at risk of coastal flooding during high tide, according to the US National Weather Service.

"It was not a typical nor'easter," said Brian Hurley, a meteorologist with the service's Weather Prediction Center in Maryland. "It's been a while since we saw one that had such a footprint in terms of power outages, that wasn't tied to a tropical system."

Strong wind gusts scoured the eastern seaboard, toppling trees and knocking down power lines. Electricity is out for more than 145,000 customers throughout Pennsylvania, according to PowerOutage.com, with over 120,000 outages in New Jersey and about 50,000 throughout New York State.

At the peak of the storm Thursday evening, weather gauges captured gusts of up to 66 miles (106 kilometers) per hour at LaGuardia Airport in New York City. In Manhattan's Central Park, top winds measured 54 miles per hour.

The gusts were too strong to safely fly gigantic balloons in the iconic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. For the first time in its history, organizers postponed the parade until Saturday morning.

articles.title: Stocks snap from a $6 trillion washout to a $3.5 trillion surge as Nvidia, Micron, and SpaceX bounce back
articles.summary: Wall Street is no longer running for the exits as chipmakers pull stocks off Wednesday's lows.
articles.body:
Wall Street is no longer running for the exits as chipmakers pull stocks off Wednesday's lows. Main Street is still headed the other way.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell almost 9% last week , its worst week since April 2025, and lost nearly $6 trillion in market value. On Monday alone, it gained about $3 trillion , putting in its best day since April 2025.

On Wednesday morning, the S&P 500 fell more than 3%, and the Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ) briefly sat 20% below its record close, the line for a bear market . That came as a hot inflation report and new tariff proposals hit. By the close, both were down less than 1%.

Friday's half-day session gave the S&P 500 its best Thanksgiving week since 2008 and its best week since April 2025, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. The index rose almost 6% for the week, while the Nasdaq 100 gained almost 7%.

Monday's surge came as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board brought back Jensen Huang at the White House's urging. "The Trump put was exercised on Monday," Interactive Brokers chief strategist Steve Sosnick told Yahoo Finance on Wednesday. "Trump put" is Wall Street's shorthand for a president who steps in when stocks fall, much like a put option protects against losses.

Chips have done the heavy lifting. Nvidia finished the week up about 20%, adding roughly $600 billion in market value. Micron ( MU ), SK Hynix ( SKHY ), AMD ( AMD ), and SanDisk ( SNDK ) closed roughly 15% to 27% above their Wednesday lows. SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) rose about 5% Friday , and Anthropic ( ANT ) jumped about 11%, climbing back above its $83 IPO price.

Everyday investors weren't the ones rushing back in. Leaving out Nvidia and Anthropic, retail traders sold a net of almost $350 million of single stocks on Monday, according to Vanda Research. It was their biggest one-day sale since March 2020, even as the Nasdaq-100 jumped almost 7%.

"The 2026 retail investor is very much a different beast, and one that is unwilling to be a buyer of last resort in an equity drawdown," Vanda's Viraj Patel wrote Wednesday.

The S&P 500 has bounced back this hard after an 8% weekly drop only seven other times since 1950. Two of the last three, in March 2020 and April 2025, marked the bottom. The other five came before more losses.

If Monday's jump can hold, history says the odds of the rally continuing improve.

Since 1993, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) has opened a Monday 2% or more higher 20 times. The five times it gave back at least half that gain by Wednesday, it broke the prior Friday's low within three months. This time, SPY gave back less than a fifth of Monday's gain by Wednesday's close. When that happened before, SPY stayed above the prior Friday's low two out of three times.

articles.title: Leo Electronics plans Rs 500 cr investment in Karnataka
articles.summary: Leo Electronics to invest Rs 500 crore in Karnataka over 10 years in 3 phases, seeking 10 acres; project to create 800 jobs, says minister M B Patil.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Japanese electronics manufacturer Leo Electronics plans to invest Rs 500 crore in Karnataka in three phases over the next 10 years, large and medium industries minister M B Patil said. articles.title: Banks Facing Bond Price-Fixing Trial Agree to Pay Over $400 Million
articles.summary: Wall Street firms including some of the industry’s biggest banks are nearing an agreement to pay more than $400 million to end a high-stakes lawsuit claiming...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Wall Street firms including some of the industry's biggest banks are nearing an agreement to pay more than $400 million to end a high-stakes lawsuit claiming they schemed to fix prices in the muni bond market.

The deal would end a long-running federal class-action suit that reached the doorstep of the US Supreme Court and was heading to a jury trial, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The proposed payment — a fraction of the billions that plaintiffs demanded — was hashed out in recent days and may be presented to a court soon, one of the people said, asking not to be identified discussing the confidential talks.

Municipalities led by Philadelphia had accused a group of banks including JPMorgan Chase & Co., Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. of colluding to set interest rates artificially high on a certain kind of debt, positioning the firms to profit at the expense of taxpayers.

Representatives for the cities and those banks declined to comment on any settlement talks. The firms have disputed the allegations in court.

A public trial threatened to place another harsh spotlight on Wall Street's treatment of Main Street, bringing with it risks of reputational damage on top of financial demands that swelled during litigation. Documents filed to the Supreme Court showed municipalities hoped to ultimately win $12 billion.

The allegations centered on so-called variable-rate demand obligations. The long-term bonds, dubbed VRDOs, have their rates periodically reset and offer investors the opportunity to return the securities for cash if they think the yields are reset too low.

The municipalities accused the banks of conspiring to inflate those rates above competitive levels to increase the chances of placing the VRDOs with an investor rather than having to keep them in their own inventory.

The claims followed findings of manipulation in the global foreign-exchange market and in setting Libor, the London interbank offered rate. Those scandals cost dozens of traders their jobs and banks billions in fines and penalties.

In their Supreme Court appeal, the banks said municipalities hadn't met one of the class-action requirements by showing that issues common to all of the plaintiffs would predominate over individual questions. The banks hoped to overturn a federal appeals court decision that let the class action go forward.

articles.title: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, halts flights and ticket sales
articles.summary: Passengers advised to seek refunds via bankruptcy process, though guarantees are not assured, warns Norse Atlantic.
articles.body:
Norwegian budget airline Norse Atlantic said it would file for bankruptcy for its main Norwegian operating unit and has stopped selling tickets, becoming the latest airline casualty of fuel-cost spikes stemming from the war in Iran..

The airline has cancelled all flights and said on its website that its customer service department is no longer available.

The shutdown came quickly. On Wednesday, the airline, which was founded in 2021, said its financial situation was “critical”. A day later, it suspended flights and warned that it could file for bankruptcy if it failed to secure funding.

By Friday, the airline said it could not raise the money it needed to continue flying.

Norse is the latest airline to struggle with rising fuel costs brought on by the US-led war in Iran. Latvia’s airBaltic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, while US budget airline Spirit Airlines went out of business in May.

Jet fuel prices have risen 71 percent globally over the past year and more than 78 percent in Europe, according to the International Air Transport Association (IATA) which tracks jet fuel prices.

“We were unable to absorb the extra cost … Fuel is what toppled this company,” CEO Eivind Roald told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK.

Norse said on its website that passengers could seek refunds through the bankruptcy process but warned that refunds were not guaranteed. It advised customers to check their travel insurance or contact their banks.

“This is a very hard day for the pilots and their families, and for all other Norse employees. Our thoughts are also with the passengers whose journeys are now cancelled,” the board of the Norse Atlantic Pilots Association told the Reuters news agency.

The airline also began ending its aircraft leasing agreements with AerCap Holdings and BOC Aviation, which were for 12 and 16 years, respectively.

Norse’s shares fell nearly 69 percent on the Oslo Stock Exchange on Friday, bringing its losses this year to 99.86 percent. In the US, its shares fell 85 percent on Friday, trading at a fraction of a cent.

articles.title: Allstate's multiday outage continues, adding to list of company tech disruptions
articles.summary: Are you in good hands? Allstate is the latest company to experience a tech outage this month.
articles.body:
Allstate ( ALL ) is the latest company to encounter a serious interruption. Since Monday, Nov. 23, the insurance company has been experiencing a multiday tech outage that has disrupted its website, mobile app, and online roadside assistance.

The company issued a statement on Wednesday, writing that customers can still contact the insurance company by phone or through local offices.

"We continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims," they wrote. "To the extent service interruptions impact a customer's ability to make a payment, they won't lose coverage or be charged late fees."

Allstate insures roughly 8 million homeowners and 26 million drivers — and some of those customers may be struggling to register a new car, close a mortgage, or get roadside help.

As of Friday morning, customers using Allstate's website for functions such as paying bills encountered a warning that they may not be able to access Allstate's services. "We're working to restore access as soon as possible," it reads.

Allstate is one of many agencies and companies — from Microsoft ( MSFT ) to Chase Bank ( JPM ) — that have experienced a tech outage during a stretch some are calling the likely worst sequence of tech outages we've had in the past 13 years .

Investors seem unfazed by the tech outage. The stock is up roughly 2% this week.

The outage comes as Allstate is reportedly cutting 5,000 jobs, nearly 10% of its workforce, "aimed at streamlining operations in an AI-driven efficiency push," according to P&C Specialist.

On the Q3 earnings call earlier this month, CEO Tom Wilson said Allstate will launch its own personal agentic assistant next year.

articles.title: Bombay HC denies relief to Tata Trusts, says Tata Sons Nov 30 meeting can go ahead but decisions taken subject to its final orders
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Friday granted no interim relief to Tata Trusts and decline to stay or defer as sought, a crucial board meeting of Tata Sons
articles.body: MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Friday granted no interim relief to Tata Trusts and decline to stay or defer as sought, a crucial board meeting of Tata Sons scheduled for November 30 which is to confirm a September 17 resolution of N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as executive chairman for the third five-year term. Justice Abhay Ahuja pronounced an operative part of the court order after a marathon hearing of interim pleas filed by two Tata Trusts. "We are not granting any relief. Let the meeting go on as scheduled. Everything—all decisions and resolutions passed at the meeting—will be subject to final orders’’, said the single Judge bench of Justice Ahuja.Tata Sons as a result can go ahead with its board meeting on Monday, even as a bitter governance battle between Tata Sons and its controlling shareholders, Tata Trusts, intensifies.Monday’s agenda includes the RBI’s listing directive, conversion of Tata Sons into a public company, changes to its articles, an EGM on N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as chairman, Shapoorji Pallonji Group’s funding request and Noel Tata’s proposal for a merger to avoid an IPO. All resolutions except the merger proposal are expected to secure a majority. Noel is expected to vote against them and Venu Srinivasan, the Trusts’ other nominee, in favour. On the merger proposal, their positions are expected to be reversed.The court asked if there was a need to defer the November 30 meeting or not permit Chandrasekaran to cast his vote as executive chairman for the second term. “His (Chandrasekaran) third term is not coming into effect on Monday, right? He is already the chairman executive now. What are the plaintiffs (trusts) anticipating will happen during the November 30 meeting,” Justice Ahuja asked.N Chandrasekaran’s term ends in February 2027. His third will start on Feb 27. The HC will next hear the matter on January 21, 2027.The HC asked for the Monday’s meeting agenda. It has critical issues both sides said. The minutes of the September 17 meeting are to be confirmed, an EGM is proposed and the RBI letters on public listing is also on the agenda, the court was informed.The two Tata Trusts—Sir Dorabjee Tata Trust (SDTT) and RDTT—and Noel Tata through a bevy of senior counsel-- AM Singhvi, Aspi Chinoy, Mukul Rohatgi and Janak Dwarkadas argued at length for an interim relief to prevent Chandrasekaran or anyone presiding as chairman to exercise the casting vote when the two Trust nominee directors Venu Srinivasan and Noel Tata—or any other appointed later-- differ during any proposals that calls for votes.Singhvi said if no interim relief is granted or Nov 30 meeting not deferred, it will “allow company to be hijacked by non-shareholders and two articles which stood the test of time for a century will be flouted repeatedly if no stay is granted on the casting vote.’’ “Like the movie Runaway Jury, it will be a runaway board,’’ he said. Chinoy said the interpretation of Article 121 to allow casting vote to decide nominee’s dissent “is absurd’’ . He said, “they are by a slight of hand destroying articles” governing the companyFriday’s interim order does not restrain Tata Sons chairman from using the casting vote for an affirmative vote when the Trust nominee directors differ as was done on September 17, when Noel Tata had dissented to Chandrasekaran’s reappointment.Tata Sons and five of its directors represented by senior counsel Harish Salve from London and senior counsel Ravi Kadam for Tata Sons, as well as Birendra Saraf for Venu Srinivasan, S Sarkar and Zal Andhyarujina for two other directors opposed grant of deferment or stay on the meeting. Salve said the real relief the Trusts want is “to run the company according to what Noel Tata wants’’.Salve said, “Noel tata wants to hold the Board hostage. It is either you go my way or the highway,’’ he said adding the Trust was rendering article 121 “sterile’’ “With two nominee directors one holds the company hostage.’’ Singhvi rejoined that his arguments “may be demolished but not caricatured’’ as attempted by Salve. Singhvi said, “It (the suit) has nothing to do with Noel Tata. Whoever it is as a nominee director. His presence has to be given meaning.’’ Dwarkadas too objected to Salve’s submission and shot back saying, “If Noel is in favour of a resolution and Srinivasan says no, what then?’’Kadam said the Trusts were challenging belatedly the September 17 decision and added that the provision for casting vote applies to both—the general vote and vote of Trust-nominees—and rebutted Singhvi’s submission that it cannot be used when nominee directors differ.Saraf submitted that Srinivasan had opposed the filing of the suit as well and argued, “Articles must be read in a manner that doesn’t bring a deadlock of Tata Sons’ functioning.” Manwani’s stand on September 17 to exercise the casting vote was “a fair and correct interpretation of the Articles. The SC ruling cited by Singhvi never interpreted the article invoked and questioned the suit’s maintainability as no Trustees were parties. The Judge took notes of submissions.Tata Trusts hold a 66% stake in Tata Sons, said Singhvi. The Trusts had filed two suits to seeks a declaration that casting vote cannot be used by the chairman when nominee directors—who stand on a different footing—differ, as Article 121 of the company’s Articles of Association (AOA) requires such nominee directors to have an affirmative vote by majority.One of two votes is “not a majority’’ the Trusts said as it challenged the September 17 board resolution for reappointment of Chandrasekaran as executive chairman.The September resolution was passed 4:1 with acting chair Harish Manwani casting the tie-breaking vote as Chandrasekaran abstained.“Tata Trusts said the battle centres around Articles 104B and 121 of Tata Sons’ AOA which call for nominee directors vote to be affirmative, by a majority. “Casting vote can never override affirmative vote,’’ said Singhvi.Salve and Kadam said the RBI had given a December 12 deadline to inform it on the listing issue. Salve said it is a 300 billion dollar company and it is not like any listing will happen in a week’’. He wondered what the Trusts’ real objection is saying even for an EGM, Trusts have the majority vote.Singhvi said Tata Sons was creating a strawman on the RBI directive, to show a fake urgency to hold the meeting.Salve added that the trusts in their interim application didn’t ask to defer the meeting. He and Andhyarujina argued that if the board meeting is held as scheduled it will cause no prejudice or irretrievable loss to the Trusts. “The two trusts cannot paralyse the company,” Salve said. Singhvi retorted, “Articles bind the company. Can they be ignored?’’ The HC will decide the Tata vs Tata tussle next year.While Tata Sons, represented by DMD Advocates was pleased with the interim order, Tata Trusts, represented by Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas (CAM) took some comfort from it despite not getting the relief they had sought. “We have got a foot in the door,” a person close to the Trusts said. “Earlier, resolutions were getting passed. This time, they will be subject to the court’s orders.”The Trusts can appeal before a division bench of the HC. They will decide their next move, said a person close to the developments.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

Game recognizes game: Legendary artist Ja Rule highlighted Warren Buffett as one of the top people he admires in the investing world.

Ja Rule has already had one remarkable career. Now he's trying to build a second one in the world of investing by leaning into what he has learned from watching Buffett and the likes of Gary Vaynerchuk.

The Queens-born rapper, born Jeffrey Atkins, became one of hip-hop's biggest stars in the early 2000s with hits like "Always on Time," "Put It on Me," and "I'm Real."

But these days, the platinum records aren't the only thing on his résumé. Ja Rule says he has invested in more than 60 companies, with several successful exits, and is increasingly focused on building wealth through startups and public-market investments.

His business interests are all over the map. He's backed the Texas Ranchers professional pickleball team and the broader pickleball business, invested in companies including SoFi ( SOFI ) and Joby Aviation ( JOBY ), and ventured into spirits with Amber & Opal whiskey and Rose Vine Cellars wine.

Of course, Ja Rule's entrepreneurial journey hasn't been without bruises. The Fyre Festival remains a major stain on his business résumé.

He soldiers on, however, with his trademark music business still doing very well on streaming platforms.

"I've already sold my records off for these songs. So this is new money for me. I get checks every month from SoundExchange off of streaming. I wasn't getting those 10 years ago," Ja Rule added.

articles.title: Govt links incentives for lithium, nickel plants to assured raw material supplies
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Companies seeking govt incentives to set up lithium and nickel processing plants will have to demonstrate assured arrangements for sourcing raw
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Companies seeking govt incentives to set up lithium and nickel processing plants will have to demonstrate assured arrangements for sourcing raw materials through offtake agreements or ownership of mines, govt has said while notifying the Rs 2,814 crore capex support scheme to promote critical mineral processing.Officials said the conditions are aimed at ensuring that companies setting up processing facilities have access to adequate raw materials to sustain operations, as India looks to reduce its dependence on imports of refined critical minerals and build domestic capabilities.The scheme, approved by the Cabinet earlier this month, provides for a 30% capital subsidy for establishing two lithium processing plants with a minimum capacity of 30,000 tonnes per annum each and two nickel processing plants with a minimum capacity of 50,000 tonnes each. The maximum support has been capped at Rs 500 crore per lithium plant and Rs 900 crore per nickel plant.Officials said the operational guidelines for the scheme were being formulated.The ministry of mines has also made it clear that entities primarily engaged in trading, simple tolling or aggregation of minerals without chemical transformation will not be eligible for financial support. Beneficiaries will also be encouraged to use indigenous technology, equipment and machinery, locally manufactured chemicals and Indian technical manpower, while prioritising sales of eligible products to domestic downstream industries at competitive prices.India is substantially dependent on imports of refined intermediates and high-purity materials for critical minerals such as lithium, nickel, cobalt, rare earth elements, platinum group elements and graphite. The processing of these minerals is geographically concentrated in a few countries, leaving supply chains vulnerable to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility and possible supply restrictions.The ministry has said high capital costs, limited availability of raw materials and constrained access to technology have made it difficult for companies to establish commercial-scale processing facilities in India without targeted support.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: High oil, gas prices add Rs 6-7 lakh crore burden to economy annually: PMO advisor
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: As India’s dependence on imported oil and gas continues to remain high, surging energy prices have added an estimated Rs 6-7 lakh crore
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As India’s dependence on imported oil and gas continues to remain high, surging energy prices have added an estimated Rs 6-7 lakh crore annually to the financial burden on the Indian economy, said Tarun Kapoor, advisor in the Prime Minister’s Office, on Friday.Speaking at the 16th Energy Security Conference organised by CII, Kapoor advocated a structural shift towards electric vehicles for both freight and passenger transportation to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels.“Our large dependence on imports has shown that we are so vulnerable that we may be caught in a tight situation and it can be disastrous for the country. High prices of crude and natural gas are costing us at least Rs 6-7 lakh crore extra every year. Imagine the impact this has on the economy,” Kapoor said.He added that if govt and oil companies had not absorbed the increase in oil and gas prices, and the higher costs had been passed on to consumers, as is done in many countries in Europe and the US, the impact on consumer goods and supplies would have been disastrous.In the first half of the 2026-27 financial year (Apr-Sept), India imported 122.7 MT of crude, marginally higher than the 121.8 MT imported during the corresponding period last year. The import bill, however, jumped to $90.6 billion from $61.9 billion due to elevated crude oil prices amid global uncertainties.Referring to the Prime Minister’s appeal to citizens to reduce energy consumption, Kapoor said some reduction was observed initially, but rising incomes, economic growth and increased travel and transportation requirements subsequently pushed consumption upwards.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Shoppers look for respite in big Black Friday discounts as inflation bites
articles.summary: By Nicholas P.
articles.body:
By Nicholas P. Brown, Arriana McLymore and Danielle Kaye

LOS ANGELES/RALEIGH, North Carolina, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Shaking off turkey hangovers, US shoppers set out on Black Friday in search of bargains robust enough to counter the pinch of stubborn inflation and high gas prices. Some said they had yet to find them.

US holiday spending — which unofficially begins on Black Friday — ‌is seen topping last year's strong figures by 4%-6%, forecasts show, but beneath top-line forecasts lie signs of stress.

Most of the gains will be attributable to inflation - which at 3.8% is about a ‌percentage point higher than in each of the last two years - and consumer sentiment remains shaky.

Chris Nile, 30, was hoping for more than the $50 discount he saw on a Nintendo Switch 2 gaming console, which brought the price to $450. "Inflation is higher - hell, even the (McDonalds) McChicken ​is up," said Nile as he shopped for his two boys at the Crabtree Valley Mall in Raleigh, North Carolina.

US store visits were tracking 2% behind last year's as of midday, at 330 million a little after 1 p.m. U.S. eastern time, according to Passby, a geospatial analytics company that measures real-time foot traffic.

Nile - like many U.S. shoppers - said he chose to bargain-hunt in person, in part to avoid shipping costs.

Marycruz Chavez, 47, said in-person shopping is a good way to spend time with her daughter - but that she ultimately expects to find better deals online.

Inflation pressure "definitely does hit a little harder" this year, said Chavez as she browsed a Los Angeles Macy's on Friday. ‌Chavez said she plans to cut "frivolous" toys and gadgets from her kids' Christmas ⁠lists.

Online spending on Black Friday was expected to jump 9.2% from a year ago to $12.9 billion, according to a forecast from Adobe Analytics, the arm of Adobe that analyzes customer behavior.

Thanksgiving Day saw consumers spend $7.1 billion online, according to Adobe, a 10.4% jump over last year, fueled by big discounts on electronics, toys and apparel.

Indeed, store ⁠visits to electronics retailer Best Buy were tracking 4.4% higher than last Black Friday at midday, according to Passby. Visits to Walmart and Target were flat to slightly up.

Overall, the National Retail Federation sees November-December holiday retail sales rising 4.2% year-over-year, to just above $1 trillion. Eventual final results often beat pre-holiday estimates.

A November survey by NRF found that 82% of consumers are taking steps to manage holiday costs, like buying less expensive gifts.

articles.title: US goods trade deficit widens 10.7% to $149.5 billion as AI boom drives record imports
articles.summary: The US goods trade deficit widened sharply in October as imports of AI-related infrastructure and other goods surged to a record high, potentially
articles.body: The US goods trade deficit widened sharply in October as imports of AI-related infrastructure and other goods surged to a record high, potentially weighing on economic growth in the fourth quarter.The goods trade deficit increased 10.7 per cent, or $14.4 billion, to $149.5 billion in October, the highest level since March 2025, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had expected a deficit of $133 billion.Imports jumped 6.1 per cent, or $21.1 billion, to a record $365.3 billion, the highest since the government began tracking the series in 1992. The increase was led by capital goods, which surged 8.5 per cent during the month and 80 per cent year-on-year, reflecting heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.Imports also rose across motor vehicles, industrial supplies and consumer goods, indicating strong domestic demand despite President Donald Trump's aggressive tariffs."The trade deficit in goods worsened in October, which will take a toll on economic growth in the fourth quarter," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS, as quoted by Reuters. "Capital goods imports are surging, showing that AI doesn't always lead to greater US economic growth."Exports of goods increased 3.2 per cent, or $6.7 billion, to $215.8 billion in October.The surge in AI-related imports could limit the technology's contribution to economic growth, despite strong corporate investment."This year's surge in capital goods imports is one reason why AI is adding less to GDP than corporate spending figures suggest," economists at Goldman Sachs wrote in a note.Trade had already subtracted 3.21 percentage points from US GDP growth in the third quarter, according to government data released on Wednesday. The drag was offset by strong consumer spending and business investment, particularly in AI-related equipment. The economy expanded at an annualised rate of 4.3 per cent in the third quarter, following 2.2 per cent growth in the previous quarter.Meanwhile, wholesale inventories rose 0.9 per cent in October after increasing 0.8 per cent in September, while retail inventories climbed 0.8 per cent following a 0.7 per cent rise in the previous month.Goldman Sachs economists lowered their fourth-quarter GDP growth estimate by 0.2 percentage point to 2.2 per cent, factoring in the October trade and inventory data.Money habits form by age 7.
